📖 How to use

  1. Enter the air temperature (°F or °C).
  2. Enter the wind speed (mph or km/h).
  3. Read the wind chill plus a frostbite warning when it is dangerously cold.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is the wind chill formula?

WC = 35.74 + 0.6215T − 35.75(V^0.16) + 0.4275T(V^0.16), with T in °F and V in mph. It is only valid for temperatures at or below 50°F (10°C) and wind speeds of 3 mph (4.8 km/h) or more.

Does wind actually lower the temperature?

Wind does not make the air colder — it strips away the thin insulating layer of warm air around exposed skin, so the body loses heat faster and skin feels (and gets) colder.

When is it dangerously cold?

The tool warns you when inputs are outside the formula's valid range. Below a −18°F (−28°C) wind chill, exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes or less.
